value.rationale: The hard cutoff of an optical Fourier pupil is a source-motivated, structurally meaningful rank erasure, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Its exact all-order GMRES failure and algorithm-independent mask-restricted geometric floor quantify the frequencies that no number of flexible right steps can restore despite invertible Tikhonov K. The discontinuous restoration of exact two-step solvability at any nonzero leakage and the inverse-leakage conditioning cost reveal a practical distinction between exact rank loss and weak transmission. This is valuable as a mathematically sharp boundary for designing/assessing idealized optical preconditioners, without asserting physical noisy-device failure.
